title: refactor(objectql): move the ReadableIds composition and permission resolution bodies out of engine.ts (#25522 cut 15)
body:
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XW9mBRdGopgsLvLN2tj9V1s)_ Part of #25522 Clause-②: no Metadata-protocol: none Ruling-ref: 6348891160 ## 维护者速读 - **改了什么**：把 `engine.ts` 里「ReadableIds 安全与权限/公式解析」一段的 8 个方法体（ReadableIds 读取范围链的组合、启动时 controlled_by_parent 主表的检查、单个父对象读取范围的询问、一次操作共享的权限解析及其三个使用方、公式故障的一次性告警）原样搬进新文件 `engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts`，类上的方法签名与注释不变，只把方法体换成转交；只被这些方法体用到的常量 `READABLE_IDS_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` 随之搬走，与留下的代码共用的 2 个工具函数和 4 个类型原地加 `export`、由新文件导入（不复制）。`engine.ts` 22,092 → 21,947 行。 - **为什么改**：#25522 按缝拆分 `engine.ts` 的第 15 刀（18.2.0 发布后重启）。缝表重测后，`validate`（约 −439）仍受 `.d.ts` 重排的裁决所限；第二名「包、应用、插件与驱动注册」（约 −233）与在途的 #26337 重叠（同一个 `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` 及其门禁），所以取不重叠的第三名。 - **风险与回滚**：纯搬移，无行为变化；公开 `.d.ts` 六个文件逐字节不变（含正控）；新文件与 `engine.ts` 互相导入（运行期循环），已用一次性探针在新旧两版构建产物上逐行对照（78 行完全一致）。回滚 = revert 本 PR。 - **先看**：`packages/objectql/src/engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts`（搬入的方法体与 `ReadableIdsPermissionFormulaHost`）、`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` 里 `composeReadableIdsChain` 的转交桩（泛型、递归经实例方法回入）与原地 `export`、`packages/core/src/security/row-serving-door-exposure.pin.test.ts`（一行改键）。 - **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`，应见全部测试文件通过。 - **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。 Cut 15 of the `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` split (#24586 ruling A, recorded in `6270097840`), the first after the release pause (`6434935278`; restart record `6439182543`, `@objectstack/spec@18.2.0`). The claim is `6439254992`. Eight bodies of the "Readable-ids security and permission/formula resolution" section move unedited into a new module, `packages/objectql/src/engine-readable-ids-permission-formula.ts`: `composeReadableIdsChain` (the chain of composed `ReadableIds` read scopes), `findUnservableControlledByParentMasters` (the boot screen over `controlled_by_parent` details), `readableIdsScopeOf` (the scope one leaf is composed with), `resolveOptionPermissions`, `permissionResolution`, `resolveFormulaPermissions` and `resolveDefaultPermissions` (an operation's one effective-permission resolution and its three consumers), and `reportFormulaFault`. No behaviour changes. #25522 stays open for the later cuts. Branch `claude/project-thread-firh6t` (the card thread's harness-pinned branch), cut from `origin/main` at `f9867020c`, which contains cut 14's merge (`00874b9e09`, #26489) and the 18.2.0 release. ## What changes ### Why this area Re-measured on `f9867020c` with cut 11's measure script and cut 14's price step (`price3.mjs`), both unchanged: a helper a paying body shares with a staying body is exported in place and blocks nothing; one read only by moving bodies moves with them. Both earlier screens still apply (query-options erasure sites, 8 at base, none in this section; module-helper closure). `engine.ts` is 22,092 lines, 7,009 of them from the last 30 days (`git blame --since=2026-09-27T10:15Z`, clone deepened to 2026-09-22 first). `scripts/pm/git-history.mjs count`: 130 commits in 30 days, 35 in 7. `class ObjectQL` holds 318 members, 255 methods and accessors. Since cut 14, one commit touched the file (#26551, +7 lines in "Action registry and activation"); the release added no new section.

| price (net lines) | section | taken? | |---|---|---| | -439 | validate | no: the `.d.ts` reorder ruling (exporting `insertStaticReadonlySubject`), unchanged since cut 14 | | -233 | Package, app, plugin and driver registration | no: overlaps open #26337, which edits `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` (read only by `registerMetadataCollections`, so it would move) and its gate row in `scripts/check-stack-collection-maps.mjs` | | -156 priced, **-145 landed** | Readable-ids security and permission/formula resolution | **yes**, without `resolveFormulaRelated` (below) | | -124 | Delete cascade and reference walking | pays less | | -71 or less | count / aggregate, Query lowering, the rest | pays less | **Why `resolveFormulaRelated` stays.** Its return type `FormulaRelated` is a non-exported type that top-level helpers that stay also use (`formulaHopScope`, `applyFormulaPlan`, `hydrateWriteFormulas` and `StoredExpressionServing`), so moving the body means exporting it in place. Measured by exporting each shared declaration on its own on the base and building (`dts-export-variant-cut15.sh`): `writeFailureLogMeta`, `isExpressionDefault`, `PermissionResolution`, `FormulaPlanEntry`, `ReadableIdsSecurity` and `ReadableIdsChain` each leave all six declaration files byte-identical; `FormulaRelated`, which names `RelatedRecordBinding` from `validation/rule-validator`, makes the declaration bundler pull the validator declarations in earlier: the same declarations in another order, with the chunk renamed (`util-DOIDsRyc` to `util-BWosSWLp`). That is the same mechanism that keeps `validate` out, and the claim's byte-identical bar forbids it, so `resolveFormulaRelated` stays (39 body lines, about -30 of the priced -156). A first full move that included it is how this was found: its build reordered the chunk, and the variant measurement named the one export responsible. ### The shape - The class keeps all eight methods with name, modifiers, signature, docblock and position. Seven bodies become one host literal of exactly the `ReadableIdsPermissionFormulaHost` members they read, plus a `.call`, marked `[#25522 cut 15]`, as cuts 8 and 10 to 14 did. Fields go as getters over a `readX` closure (`_registry`, `logger`, `_effectiveObjectPermissionsResolver`, `formulaFaultReported`); methods go as late-bound closures (`refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses`, `readableIdsScopeOf`, `composeReadableIdsChain`, `uncomposableReadableIdsParent`, `buildEvalUser`, `defaultFieldEntries`), so a spy or double set on the engine is still the one a call reaches. No moved body assigns a field, so there is no setter (cut 13's setter ruling has nothing to apply to). - `composeReadableIdsChain` is generic and recursive: its stub calls the function instantiated with its type parameter `N` and `.call`s it on the host, the spelling #25467's generic cuts used, and the host's `composeReadableIdsChain` closure re-enters through the method, so the recursion still passes the instance (the probe counts both levels). - `resolveOptionPermissions` reads no member of the class, so its method calls the function directly (`return resolveOptionPermissions(schema, payloads, resolution);`). - **Helpers and types, under the cut-14 seat ruling.** `READABLE_IDS_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` is read only by `composeReadableIdsChain`, so it moved with it, docblock included and byte for byte. `writeFailureLogMeta` (read too by `reportFindFailure`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`) and `isExpressionDefault` (`applyFieldDefaults`) stay where they were, byte for byte, and gain `export` in place; so do the types the moved bodies share with staying code: `PermissionResolution`, `FormulaPlanEntry`, `ReadableIdsSecurity` and `ReadableIdsChain` (each `export` alone was measured `.d.ts`-neutral, above). `UnservableControlledByParentMaster` was already exported. The module imports the two functions as values and the five types as types from `./engine.js`; it is a new module, so before that it imported nothing from `./engine.js`. `index.ts` and `core.ts` name their exports singly, so nothing new is published (below). - **The run-time cycle (measured).** That value import makes `engine.ts` and the module import each other. The module runs nothing at evaluation (declarations only), and `engine.ts` imports it right after `./engine-master-detail-related.js`, after every module the moved bodies import, so the evaluation order of every other module is unchanged. Measured on the built bundles (`index.mjs`, `core.mjs`, `index.js`, `core.js`): with the `// src/engine.ts` region markers set aside, the `// src/...` region order at head equals the base's with one line added, the new module, between `engine-master-detail-related` and `in-memory-aggregation`. One `engine.ts` region disappears: the one that held only the external `@objectstack/spec/data` import of `ReadableIds`, `RLS_DENY_FILTER`, `markFilterSubtreeProvenance` and `isControlledByParentMasterField`, whose readers all moved; that import now sits in the module's region (an external package already loaded by earlier regions; ESM imports are hoisted). The bundles hold both files in one module, so the published build has no cycle. The late-binding probe answers the same on base and head (Tests). - **Imports.** The module imports `ReadableIds`, `RLS_DENY_FILTER`, `isControlledByParentMasterField`, `markFilterSubtreeProvenance`, `FilterCondition` (type), `ExecutionContext` (type), `toEvalPermissions`, `EvalError` and `EvalPermissions` (types), `collectComposableReadableIds`, `composeReadableIdsLeaves`, `describeReadableIdsLeaf`, `readableIdsRefusalError`, `ComposableReadableIdsSite` (type), `optionVisibilityReadsPermissions` and `readsPermissionPredicate`. `engine.ts` drops `composeReadableIdsLeaves`, the whole `ReadableIds` / `RLS_DENY_FILTER` / `markFilterSubtreeProvenance` / `isControlledByParentMasterField` import line, and `toEvalPermissions`, whose last readers moved. It keeps `optionVisibilityReadsPermissions` and `readsPermissionPredicate`: no code in `engine.ts` reads them any more, but the docblocks that stay on `resolveOptionPermissions` and `resolveFormulaPermissions` `{@link}` them, the same use `DatasourceUnavailableError` already has there at base (TypeScript counts a `{@link}` as a use under `noUnusedLocals`), and that import line stays byte-identical. - The module header names what moved, what stays and why, and how the helpers were handled. ### Net lines (the seat's rule) `engine.ts` goes from 22,092 to 21,947 lines, **net -145** (59 added, 204 removed). The module is 362 lines. With the one path reader below, the diff against `origin/main` is 628 changed lines over 3 files (+423 / -205). ### Readers of the moved lines - `packages/core/src/security/row-serving-door-exposure.pin.test.ts` lists every non-test file that calls a security service's `canReadObject(`. `engine.ts`'s only call was in `readableIdsScopeOf`, so its row moves to the new module, with its `not-a-door` classification and reason unchanged (the reason already described exactly this ask: "the ReadableIds composition (ADR-0139 D2) …"). Without the re-key the census would read `engine.ts` as stale and the module as unclassified. - No other census, ADR anchor, docs row or test key names a moved member or helper by `engine.ts` path: `objectql/src/engine.ts#NAME` pointers under `packages/spec/**`, `docs/**`, `content/**` and `scripts/**` name none of them; `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` and its `NON_READ_ANCHORS` have no row for them (no moved body reads `isSystem`); `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts` keys none of them (its `resolveFormulaRelated` row stays with that body in `engine.ts`); no moved body calls `referenceTargetOf(` (core's `second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` is unchanged); no moved body holds a `query-options/no-any-erasure` site (8 at base and head), a tenant-audit untyped receiver or a private static read. Mentions by bare name (plugin-security's `READABLE_IDS_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` comments, `plugin.ts`'s `ObjectQL#findUnservableControlledByParentMasters`) name the constant and the method, which still exist under those names. - **No ADR anchor paragraph describes a moved body** (the `engine.ts` entry is the transaction-seam paragraph), so the module needs no anchor entry of its own. - **Read-seam census (the cut-21 trap of #25467).** `check-durability-degradation-log-level --list` at base and head is identical once line numbers are masked: 48 durability seams and 82 read seams, the same entries. No moved body is named in a read-seam entry. - **Decision-letter count:** `check-adr-anchors` at base `f9867020c` (clean detached worktree): 91 anchored files, **1,881** decision-letter citations on the anchored surface, 59,819 resolving citations across 8,353 files. At head: 91 anchored files, **1,880**, 59,820 across 8,354. The one letter that leaves the anchored surface is `[ADR-0139 D6, as amended — the nested master chain]` in `READABLE_IDS_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH`'s docblock, which moved with the constant into the module, which no anchor entry names; the citation still resolves (it is in the 59,820), it is just no longer counted on the anchored surface. The +1 resolving citation and +1 file are the new module (its header names ADR-0139 once). The same one-letter move was disclosed on cuts 8 and 12 of #25467; anchoring the module to keep the count would mean writing a new invariant paragraph, which is not a move. ## Why #25522 splits `engine.ts` one seam at a time so that a change to one area reads, reviews and conflicts as that area alone. This cut takes the section that pays most under this cut's rulings and that no open PR touches (table above). Nothing about what the engine does changes. ## Tests No test is added or changed apart from the re-keyed row above: the move is proved by identity, not by new behaviour.
Public .d.ts byte-identical, with a positive control Built `@objectstack/objectql` at the base (`f9867020c`, `engine.ts` blob `9c44e9da88b5`) and at head (`engine.ts` blob `19a84bece0b0`), each from a clean tree (`dts-cut15.sh`), and hashed every declaration file. So the comparison sees a one-word change to a moved member's signature. The restore leg put the blob back to `19a84bece0b0` (`git diff HEAD` empty), and the head was rebuilt before every later step.
AST compare (move-only) `astcmp.mjs` (TypeScript compiler API, comments and whitespace ignored, tokens compared) on base `engine.ts` against head `engine.ts` plus the module: - Moved bodies, all eight **SAME** (parameters, return type, type parameters, `async`, body tokens, and every body line equal after one level of indent): `composeReadableIdsChain` 380 tokens / 46 lines, `findUnservableControlledByParentMasters` 201 / 12, `readableIdsScopeOf` 253 / 29, `resolveOptionPermissions` 149 / 19, `permissionResolution` 80 / 11, `resolveFormulaPermissions` 178 / 25, `reportFormulaFault` 101 / 14, `resolveDefaultPermissions` 223 / 21. - `class ObjectQL`: 318 of 318 members kept, in the same order; 310 byte-identical, and the 8 stubs keep docblock, modifiers and signature identical. - Top level: 217 of 228 base statements byte-identical. The other 11 (`exportcmp.mjs`): the 3 import edits above; 6 declarations that gained `export` and are otherwise byte-identical with their leading docblocks (`writeFailureLogMeta`, `isExpressionDefault`, `PermissionResolution`, `FormulaPlanEntry`, `ReadableIdsSecurity`, `ReadableIdsChain`); `READABLE_IDS_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH`, byte-identical in the module (1,137 characters with its docblock); and the class. The head adds one statement, the module import.
Late-binding probe (base and head dist) `zz-probe-cut15.mjs` (a one-off, not committed) loads the built `ObjectQL` and drives all eight methods with doubles set on the instance for every member the hosts read (`_registry`, `logger`, `_effectiveObjectPermissionsResolver`, `formulaFaultReported`, `refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses`, `readableIdsScopeOf`, `composeReadableIdsChain`, `uncomposableReadableIdsParent`, `buildEvalUser`, `defaultFieldEntries`, plus `hasObjectMiddleware` and `resolveDatasourceBinding` under them), then prints results, the call order on the doubles and the log lines. Cases: the `ReadableIds` chain through `composeReadableIdsAtBoundary` (a nested two-level chain, which re-enters `composeReadableIdsChain` through the instance; a cycle, refused; a denied parent; no restriction; `getReadFilter` throwing; the admission throwing; the `explain` fallback; the deny sentinel; a non-filter answer; a `readableIdsScopeOf` double replaced after construction); `findUnservableControlledByParentMasters` over both D5 classes; `permissionResolution` with no user, with a user (asked once for two `get()`s) and with no resolver; `resolveOptionPermissions`, `resolveFormulaPermissions` and `resolveDefaultPermissions` with no resolution, a resolution and a throwing one; `reportFormulaFault` twice on one pair (one line), and with a `formulaFaultReported` double set after construction. The 78 output lines are identical on base and head (the engine's own construction log lines, which carry timestamps, set aside), which is the check the seat's ruling asks for on the run-time cycle. The module-order measurement on the bundles is under "The run-time cycle" above.
